name: Smärky Kanum
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Only survey wordlists/notes (Donohue) known; no published phonology or stress description located

new_statements.quote: [p.58] Berdasarkan data, walaupun dalam bahasa Kanum Barkari terdapat unsur-unsur suprasegmental berupa tekanan, nada, dan durasi, akan tetapi tidak terdapat unsur suprasegmental yang distingtif atau yang membedakan makna. Oleh sebab itu, dapat disimpulkan bahwa dalam bahasa Kanum Barkari tidak terdapat fonem suprasegmental. Mengenai unsur suprasegmental yang berupa durasi selalu jatuh pada suku terbuka yang dibunyikan panjang. [p.54] Fonem /e/ akan terealisasi menjadi [e] apabila berada pada suku kata terbuka yang mendapat tekanan. Fonem /e/ akan terealisasi menjadi [ә] apabila berada di luar lingkungan tersebut.
new_statements.translation: [p.58] Based on the data, although Kanum Barkari has suprasegmental features of stress, pitch and duration, there is no suprasegmental feature that is distinctive, i.e. that differentiates meaning. It can therefore be concluded that Kanum Barkari has no suprasegmental phonemes. As for the suprasegmental feature of duration, it always falls on open syllables, which are pronounced long. [p.54] The phoneme /e/ is realised as [e] when it stands in an open syllable that receives stress. /e/ is realised as [ə] outside that environment.
new_statements.citation: Iribaram, Siti Masitha. 2015. Fonem segmental bahasa Kanum Barkari. Gramatika: Jurnal Ilmiah Kebahasaan dan Kesastraan 3(1): 47-59. Kantor Bahasa Provinsi Maluku Utara. DOI 10.31813/gramatika/3.1.2015.120.47--59.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress exists (stressed vs unstressed open syllables condition vowel and consonant allophones, e.g. /e/ -> [e] under stress, [ə] elsewhere) but is not contrastive; the article never says which syllable carries it. No placement rule can be extracted. (Independent data point, not a statement: the SIL 2009 Rawa Biru Smärky wordlist marks stress on the first syllable in 116 of 127 marked polysyllables, the rest on the second syllable mostly after an initial schwa.)
new_statements.exceptions: None; only that duration (length) goes with open syllables.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation-form words elicited in Kondo village (Barkari/Barkali dialect, bark1251); word-level phonemic analysis, no phrase-level discussion.
new_statements.identity_note: The only first-hand phonology found describes 'Kanum Barkari' as spoken in Kampung Kondo (Distrik Naukenjerai) = Glottolog dialect Barkali [bark1251] under Smärky Kanum [smar1235]. Carroll 2016 (pp. 6-7, Table 1.1) treats 'Smerky' as one of three Kanum languages, comprising Smerky proper (Rawa Biru, Tomer, Tomerau), Taemer (Yanggandur) and Barkari (Rawa Biru/Yakiw) as a dialect chain; Iribaram herself (cited in Sanjoko 2016 p. 2) says Barkari differs from 'Kanum Smarky'. Glottolog's other smar1235 item, the 2021 Kamus Tamer, covers the Taemer/Ngkantia [ngka1237] dialect. The SIL 2009 wordlist evidence is for Smärky proper at Rawa Biru. Sister language Ngkolmpu = ngka1235 (Carroll) is a separate languoid and its sources were read only for context.

sources.note: p.58 (Penutup): stress, pitch and duration exist but none is distinctive; concludes there are no suprasegmental phonemes; duration falls on open syllables. pp.53-54: several vowel/consonant allophones are conditioned by 'open syllable that receives stress' vs not. Nowhere states which syllable is stressed.

sources.citation: Sohn, Myo-Sook, Randy Lebold & Ron Kriens. 2009. Report on the Merauke Subdistrict Survey, Papua, Indonesia. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2009-018 (46 pp.).
sources.note: No prose on stress. Appendix V 239-item wordlist for Rawa Biru (Smärky Kanum) is transcribed with IPA stress marks: by my scripted tally 127 of 134 polysyllabic forms are marked, 116 with initial stress (87 of 2-syll, 24 of 3-syll, 5 of 4-syll), 11 with second-syllable stress (mostly after a schwa first syllable, e.g. pəˈʈʌɭ, kəˈjʌŋ, seˈmɛlku). Data only, not a statement.
